content:
Maria: quick post-mortem — we had a near-OOM event on the us-west-2 dedicated GPU pool at ~07:12 UTC. Symptoms: increased queuing, token throttling, and a spike in 504s for ~18m.
Otto: saw the alerts. What pushed usage over the threshold?
Maria: short summary: traffic burst from a single heavy-embedding job + autoscaler lag. The job requested large batch sizes and pinned high-quant models.
Kevin: can you paste the allocation snapshot?
Maria: sure — grabbing from the controller logs.
Maria: ```
controller: summary at 07:13: total_gpus=120 allocated=118 free=2 pending_pods=14
node_pressure: two nodes at 98% gpu_mem, one node OOM-killed 07:14:22 (evicted pod rtx-32g-job-7)
queue: avg_latency_tokens 480ms -> 2.3s during spike
rate_limit: per-customer throttle engaged for cx-457 (backpressure)
```
Priya: the evicted pod was the embedder job from cx-457?
Maria: yes — it was a long-running batched embedder, 1024 sequence length, batch=64, model=xlarge-quant; it started retries which created more parallelism.
Otto: autoscaler timeline?
Maria: autoscaler noticed CPU/GPU pressure at 07:12:30, started scale-up, but new nodes registered ~07:20 due to provisioning + image pull (8m).
Kevin: so two contributors: one noisy tenant + slow node provisioning. Any networking issues?
Maria: we saw slightly elevated image-pull times in us-west-2 registry (~120s) vs usual ~18s. This added to startup delay.
SRE-Bot: incident created: INC-2024-211 at 07:16 UTC — severity: high.
Priya: did the scheduler try to binpack smaller jobs differently? Any preemption policy triggered?
Maria: preemption enabled but we set avoid-preempt label on dedicated pool for enterprise SLAs; so no preemption occurred. That was intentional but meant long jobs couldn't be displaced.
Otto: cost question — were these reserved jobs or on-demand?
Maria: customer workload ran on dedicated reserved pool (Committed), so cost not the immediate concern but availability was.
Kevin: what about KV cache pressure? Any cache thrashing?
Maria: KV cache blowouts seen on two pods — they hit memory limits, causing thrash and additional OOM kills.
Priya: lessons?
Maria: initial list: 1) tighten per-tenant concurrent batch limits for embedding workloads, 2) faster fallback to a quantized smaller model when memory pressure detected, 3) reduce image size / use warm image cache in us-west-2, 4) revisit preemption policy for emergency reclaim, 5) add early throttling signals upstream (ingress) based on GPU mem headroom.
Otto: agree. Also add autoscaler tuning: lower target CPU/GPU threshold to trigger earlier scale-up, and implement node warm pool with 2-3 hot nodes per AZ.
Kevin: can we implement an admission controller that blocks giant batch sizes for dedicated pools? simple validation rule.
Maria: yes — already prototyping: reject batch>32 for embeddings on dedicated unless whitelisted.
Priya: action items and owners?
Maria: AI: Maria — push model-fallback prototype (ETA 2w). Otto — autoscaler tuning + warm pool (ETA 1w). Kevin — admission controller rule + rollout (ETA 3d). Priya — add observability: token-level GPU headroom metric + dashboard (ETA 4d).
Otto: I'll also add a runbook step: when queue latency >1s and free_gpus<5, enable emergency-preempt toggle (manual) and notify SRE.
Deploy-Bot: rollout deployed: admission-controller v0.1 -> canary on one node group at 08:30 UTC.
Priya: follow-up: we should schedule a capacity forecast review — the spike was ~2.3x expected for that hour; we need seasonal buffer for monthly demo days.
Kevin: agree — propose +20% buffer for Q3 and a dedicated warm pool per region.
Maria: closing notes: incident severity downgraded 07:30 after scale-up and manual throttles; no customer data loss, degraded latency only. Documented the retro and action items above. :thumbsup:
Otto: thanks — will create tickets and link to INC-2024-211.
Kevin: thanks everyone.
Maria: adding logs and graphs to the incident doc in #incidents: INC-2024-211.
